The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=a is given by

P4(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+f(4)(a)4!(x−a)4.

Here, we have a=1, so

P4(x)=f(1)+f′(1)(x−1)+f″(1)2!(x−1)2+f‴(1)3!(x−1)3+f(4)(1)4!(x−1)4.

So we need to work out f(1), f′(1), f″(1), f‴(1) and f(4)(1), as follows: f(x)=ln⁡x⟹f(1)=ln⁡1=0f′(x)=1x=x−1⟹f′(1)=1−1=1f″(x)=−x−2⟹f″(1)=−(1)−2=−1f‴(x)=−(−2)x−3=2x−3⟹f‴(1)=2(1)−3=2f(4)(x)=2(−3)x−4=−6x−4⟹f(4)(1)=−6(1)−4=−6

Therefore, P4(x) is given by

P4(x)=0+(x−1)−12!(x−1)2+23!(x−1)3−64!(x−1)4=(x−1)−12(x−1)2+13(x−1)3−14(x−1)4.
